### workspace workflow insights --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow insights ID [--limit N] [--last DURATION] [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]

Show where a workflow's recent runs keep retrying, being rejected or stopping.

ID is a workflow definition id; it need not exist now. Reads the newest runs of that id (--limit, default 20), going and
finished, in every workspace unless --name or --project narrows it. Read only: it writes nothing and prints counts and run
ids, never a reviewer's write-up, a summary or a prompt. Use the ids with `workflow trace RUN`.

Sections: hot steps (retried or resumed, with the runs and the token mean), repeated rejections (a step, a reviewer and
the verdict reject, or a reviewer's problem code), failed attempts by step and code, holds (budget_spent, run_timed_out,
failed_check) and the effect of each definition, version and pack text, from `workflow compare`, with its warning.

Thresholds: with fewer than 3 runs it prints "Not enough runs" and no rankings. A rejection theme needs the same key in
3 different runs; three rejections in one run count once, and anything less is listed as a single observation.
The store keeps the newest 200 finished runs across all workflows, so older runs may be gone.

Exit codes: 0 (also when the workflow has no runs), 1 for a usage error, 3 with status partial when a run file cannot be read,
since the figures are then incomplete.

Options:
    --limit N                    Read this many of the newest runs (a whole number from 1; default 20)
    --last DURATION              Only runs started in the last DURATION (30d, 2w, 12h, 90m); a bare number means seconds
    --name NAME                  Only that workspace's runs
    --project [NAME]             Only that project's runs (NAME, or the project of the current workspace)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow insights rpiv    # where the last 20 runs of rpiv went wrong
  workspace workflow insights rpiv --limit 50 --last 30d    # up to 50 runs, from the last 30 days
  workspace workflow insights rpiv --project --json    # for a script: sections with run ids and next_actions
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow learn --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow learn reflect RUN [--agent KIND] [--json]

Ask an agent in a new pane to look back at a finished run and write reflection.md.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).

RUN must be finished (completed, failed or cancelled; a run still going is refused with run_not_finished). Opens a new split
pane in the run's workspace and types one line into it that points at instructions the command writes to
reflection.prompt.md in the run's evidence directory. The agent reads the run's recorded evidence, which the instructions fence as
data, and writes reflection.md next to it. The run's own pane is never used and the run is not changed.

The pane is bound with kind reflection and a guard keeps its file tools to that one reflection.md. This is a tripwire,
not a sandbox: shell commands are not covered. The binding ends when the agent's turn ends with the file written, or
with the session; end it sooner with `workspace binding clear --pane ID` or by closing the pane. While it lasts, a second
reflection on the same run is refused with reflection_in_progress and plan start and spine start do not type into the pane.

When reflection.md already exists the command prints its text and path and starts nothing; delete the file to reflect again.
reflection.md and reflection.prompt.md live in the run's evidence directory, <state dir>/.workflows/evidence/RUN/ (the
state dir is ~/.local/state/workspace unless XDG_STATE_HOME says otherwise). Nothing ever reads reflection.md into another
prompt, and it is removed with the run's evidence.

Options:
    --agent KIND                 The coding agent the pane runs: claude, codex, opencode, pi (default: the workspace's main agent)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow learn reflect wr_261117195535omsd    # start a reflection pane on a finished run, or print the one already written
  workspace workflow learn reflect wr_261117195535omsd --agent claude    # choose the agent kind instead of the workspace's main agent
  workspace workflow learn reflect wr_261117195535omsd --agent codex --json    # for a script: the pane id and the path the agent will write
--- stderr
--- end

Usage: workspace workflow learn reflect RUN [--agent KIND] [--json]

Ask an agent in a new pane to look back at a finished run and write reflection.md.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).

RUN must be finished (completed, failed or cancelled; a run still going is refused with run_not_finished). Opens a new split
pane in the run's workspace and types one line into it that points at instructions the command writes to
reflection.prompt.md in the run's evidence directory. The agent reads the run's recorded evidence, which the instructions fence as
data, and writes reflection.md next to it. The run's own pane is never used and the run is not changed.

The pane is bound with kind reflection and a guard keeps its file tools to that one reflection.md. This is a tripwire,
not a sandbox: shell commands are not covered. The binding ends when the agent's turn ends with the file written, or
with the session; end it sooner with `workspace binding clear --pane ID` or by closing the pane. While it lasts, a second
reflection on the same run is refused with reflection_in_progress and plan start and spine start do not type into the pane.

When reflection.md already exists the command prints its text and path and starts nothing; delete the file to reflect again.
reflection.md and reflection.prompt.md live in the run's evidence directory, <state dir>/.workflows/evidence/RUN/ (the
state dir is ~/.local/state/workspace unless XDG_STATE_HOME says otherwise). Nothing ever reads reflection.md into another
prompt, and it is removed with the run's evidence.

Options:
    --agent KIND                 The coding agent the pane runs: claude, codex, opencode, pi (default: the workspace's main agent)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow learn reflect wr_261117195535omsd    # start a reflection pane on a finished run, or print the one already written
  workspace workflow learn reflect wr_261117195535omsd --agent claude    # choose the agent kind instead of the workspace's main agent
  workspace workflow learn reflect wr_261117195535omsd --agent codex --json    # for a script: the pane id and the path the agent will write

### workspace workflow sweep --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow sweep [RUN | --name WORKSPACE] [--budget-only | --scheduled] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow sweep --install | --uninstall [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow sweep --installed [--json]

One pass over the runs going: act on the ones that have stopped.

Looks at every run still going (or one RUN, or one workspace's) and, for a step an agent should be
working on: records a pane or agent that is gone (`step_stalled`; the run keeps its checkout until you
resume or cancel it), starts a workspace's agent daemon that is not running, decides a step whose agent
ended its turn unseen, and applies the step's `on_timeout` (`interrupt` presses the agent's interrupt
keys once; `fail` fails the step; `warn`, the default, does nothing). A turn counts as unseen once the pane has
been idle for the definition's `stall`; with no `stall` and no `on_timeout`, only a gone pane or agent and
a missing daemon are acted on. A step whose line was never delivered, when the failure proves nothing
was typed (pane busy, no daemon socket), is typed again once the pane is idle, after 1, 5, then 15
minutes each time, up to the definition's `redeliver` times (default 10, 0 turns it off); a retried attempt does
not count against max_attempts, and when the retries run out the run waits for you. Nothing retries
unless something runs the sweep; the installed entry and an agent daemon with a run going each run it
every 300 seconds, so the 1 minute backoff can wait up to 5. A held step, a parked resume and a
running check are left alone.

When a step's agent exited or its pane is gone and its tmux session runs, the sweep schedules a restart
(row action infra_retry_scheduled). After 60 seconds, then 300 and 900, the step starts again in a new
Claude Code pane (the agent daemon's `workflow advance` does it), up to workflows.infra_retry.max times
(default 2, 0 turns it off). When they run out the row action is infra_retries_exhausted: run
`workflow resume RUN` (`--restart-step` for a new attempt) or `workflow cancel RUN`.

It needs no agent daemon, so a scheduler can run it; a workspace's agent daemon also runs it for its
own workspace every 5 minutes while a run is going. Running it twice records nothing twice. A run
that another process is changing is skipped and looked at on the next pass. A daemon that could not be
started, a failed interrupt, a missing program or an unreadable run file is a failed result (exit 3, or
1 when every result failed). See docs/README.workflow.md.

To run it on a schedule even with no agent daemon, --install writes a per-user LaunchAgent (every 5
minutes) and loads it; it is never done for you. --uninstall unloads and removes it, --installed says whether it is there and loaded.
The entry records the absolute Ruby, program and PATH it was installed with, so run --install again
after a Ruby or install move. The entry's output goes to sweep.log in the state directory
(~/.local/state/workspace, or $XDG_STATE_HOME/workspace); a pass trims that log to its last 256 KiB when it is over 1 MiB, and writes
.workflows/sweep-last.json there (the last pass, and the last unfiltered one). An entry
installed before that reads as out of date (up_to_date false) until --install runs again.
A plist that is not ours is never touched.

Next actions:
With --json, next_actions (always present, empty when nothing needs a person) lists what a person can run.
`workflow resume RUN` for a held step or a recorded stall (with the extra-tokens or extra-time need when a
limit is spent, or a pane need for a held retry), `workflow cancel RUN`, `launch WORKSPACE` for a stopped
workspace, `focus WORKSPACE --pane PANE` for a pane waiting on an answer, and `workflow sweep` after a
--dry-run. Each carries the result's reason (or cause) as why.

Options:
    --name WORKSPACE             Only this workspace's runs (default: every run going)
    --dry-run                    Say what would be done and do nothing (also for --install and --uninstall; refused with --installed)
    --install                    Install and load the launchd entry that runs the sweep every 5 minutes (opt-in)
    --uninstall                  Unload and remove that entry
    --installed                  Say whether that entry is installed and loaded; changes nothing
    --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md), one result per run looked at, and next_actions
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow sweep --dry-run    # which stopped runs would a sweep act on?
  workspace workflow sweep    # act on every run that has stopped
  workspace workflow sweep RUN    # only this run
  workspace workflow sweep --name app.worktree-x --json    # for a script: one result per run in that workspace
  workspace workflow sweep --install --dry-run    # what would installing the 5-minute schedule do?
  workspace workflow sweep --installed    # is the schedule installed and loaded?
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow recover --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow recover [--dry-run] [--json]

Bring going runs back after a reboot.

After a reboot or the loss of the tmux server, restores each workspace that has a going run no person
is holding, restarts a step that was mid-turn (a new attempt with a fresh conversation, in the run's own pane), and wakes a run that was
between turns (reviewing, checking, a retry backoff). It goes through runs oldest first, one workspace at a time.

Run `workspace workflow recover --dry-run` first: it lists each run and what would happen, and changes nothing.
Restoring a workspace also brings back its other recorded agent panes, not only the run's.

Each run gets one result (restarted, restored, skipped, refused, failed). Skipped means nothing needed
doing or a person holds the run. Refused and failed mean the run is still stopped, and the row names the
command to run. With --json, next_actions lists those commands. Exit status: 0, 3 when some results
failed or were refused, 1 when all were.

A run is restarted at most workflows.recover.max_per_run times (default 2; set it with `workspace config
set workflows.recover.max_per_run N`), so a run that keeps dying is left for you.

Options:
    --dry-run                    Say what would be done and do nothing
    --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md), one result per going run, and next_actions
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow recover --dry-run    # which going runs would be brought back?
  workspace workflow recover    # restore their workspaces and restart or wake them
  workspace workflow recover --json    # for a script: one result per run
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow resume --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow resume [RUN] [--from STEP | --restart-step] [--note TEXT] [--pane PANE] [--extra-attempts N] [--extra-tokens N] [--extra-time DURATION] [--extra-rounds N] [--json]
       workspace workflow resume [RUN] --accept-guard --note WHY [--retry] [--pane PANE] [--extra-attempts N] [--extra-tokens N] [--extra-time DURATION] [--json]

Get a run going again.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).
With RUN left out, the run this pane is bound to is used, else the one run going in this checkout; several going runs refuse with ambiguous_run and RUN is needed.

Asks for its lock again, runs a failed or undelivered step again, looks again at a step whose files
were missing, or moves it to the workspace's Claude pane when its own is gone. --from at a waiting
gate is refused from a pane a run is bound to.

A run waiting at a gate is approved or rejected instead; resume needs --from there. It types the
step into the run's pane again unless an agent is still working on it, or its check is running (then
it does nothing and says so). Use it for a run `workflow status` shows as stuck.

While the run is paused, resume is refused with `run_paused`: run `workspace workflow unpause RUN` instead.

Run from the pane it would type into (an agent resuming its own run) it types nothing: the answer is
`parked`, exit 0, and the caller should end its turn. The agent daemon carries it out once the turn
is over, within 1 hour, else the run reads waiting_you / parked_timeout. It needs a daemon started
after the upgrade (workspace daemon restart) and a pane in window 0. With a draft in a Claude pane's
input box nothing is typed and the draft stays (pane_busy, input_not_empty).

After a resume that did not go straight through, one sentence says what the run waits for: a parked
resume (the pane and when the park expires), a retry backoff (when the step starts again), a pane that
looked busy (why), or nothing (the "Nothing was done" message stands in for the sentence). The sentence is the
only place the pane, the time and the refusal are said; times are local. --json has the same as `waits`,
null when the resume went through.

On a step being reviewed (reviewing) it never runs the author again: a round still running is left
alone, a round stopped for a person starts again as a fresh round (spending one of the step's
rounds), and --from ends the round and closes its review window first. It is not parked then, and
--from from the run's own pane is refused (step_reviewing). Once the step has spent its
review.max_rounds, a resume that would start another round, or run again a step its last round
rejected, is refused (review_rounds_spent) unless --extra-rounds N adds N to the step's rounds (N
must cover the overrun; the refusal names the least). --from still goes on, and cancel ends the run.

A resume that would start an attempt is refused (attempts_spent) when the run has made all its
max_attempts, or (step_attempts_spent) when the step it would run has made all its own max_attempts;
--extra-attempts N adds N to the run's allowance and to that step's, and goes on. N must cover the overrun
(1 for a run exactly spent; the refusal names the least). It is ignored when the resume starts no attempt.

A run held by its definition's budget (reason budget_spent) is refused the same way (budget_spent)
until --extra-tokens N adds N to its token budget; the total counted is a minimum, since sub-agents
and attempts with no usage are left out.

A run held by its definition's timeout: (reason run_timed_out) is refused the same way (run_timed_out)
until --extra-time DURATION adds to its timeout. Only active time counts against it: time a person
is waited on (a gate, a parked resume, a held budget, a failed check), time the machine was off or
asleep, and time a step spent stalled do not. With the budget and the timeout both spent, pass both
flags.

--restart-step is for a step whose agent or pane crashed. It ends the unfinished attempt as interrupted (it
still counts toward max_attempts and the budget) and types the step again into a Claude Code pane in a fresh
conversation, starting with a short summary of the current commit and the plan's tasks. It is typed into the
run's pane if its agent is idle there, otherwise into the one free idle Claude Code pane of the workspace, or
the one named with --pane. Run it as a person from another pane than the run's own. --note, --pane and
--extra-attempts, --extra-tokens and --extra-time still work. It can not be combined with --from,
--accept-guard, --retry or --extra-rounds (use one or the other). Refusals, each ending "Nothing was changed.":
  the step has nothing running to restart (no_open_attempt);
  its agent is still working, or its line is still being typed (step_still_working): wait, then run it again;
  several idle Claude Code panes could take it (pane_ambiguous): name one with --pane;
  no Claude Code pane is free to take it (no_agent_pane): start one, or name one with --pane;
  the pane is mid-turn, or a pane named with --pane is the caller's, a review pane or another run's (pane_busy);
  the unfinished attempt could not be closed (restart_not_closed): run it again;
  the run or the step has used all its attempts (attempts_spent, step_attempts_spent) or the token budget
  (budget_spent): add --extra-attempts or --extra-tokens.

A plain resume of such a crashed step prints a hint to use --restart-step (stderr; `hint` with --json).
A person's resume also gives the step a fresh set of automatic restarts (workflows.infra_retry.max).

--accept-guard takes a guard stop (failed_check by head_moved, hooks_changed, hidden_changed,
no_commit, operation_in_progress or tracked_changed) as a person's decision; any other stop is
refused (guard_not_stopped). It needs --note WHY, and is refused from a pane bound to a run. HEAD
now becomes the run's base_sha and the guard's snapshot is taken again (guard_base_unreadable, and
nothing changed, when it can't be read). Only the guard is accepted: the step's produces files,
require: proofs and status: check still run, and only when they pass does its attempt read overridden
and the step pass (its review round or gate still applies); else it stops on their reason. With
--retry the step runs again as a new attempt instead, counted against max_attempts; refused
(guard_cannot_pass) while no_commit or operation_in_progress would stop it again. --from can't go
with it. Later guarded steps measure from the new base. The note is recorded on a guard_overridden
event and given to the next attempt, after a line naming the guard and the new base.

Options:
    --from STEP                  Start again at this step
    --restart-step               Start a crashed step again in a fresh conversation
    --note TEXT                  Added to the next attempt's instructions
    --pane PANE                  The pane to run in (%19 or 0.1) instead of the workspace's Claude pane
    --extra-attempts N           Add N (a whole number from 1 up) to the run's attempt allowance, for a run or step that has spent max_attempts; N must cover the overrun (1 for a run exactly spent), and the refusal names the least
    --extra-tokens N             Add N (a whole number from 1 up) to the run's token budget, for a run that has used budget.tokens; N must cover the overrun, and the refusal names the least and a round figure
    --extra-time DURATION        Add DURATION (30m, 2h, or seconds) to the run's timeout, for a run that has used its timeout: (active time is the time the machine was up, less waits for a person, stalls and downtime); DURATION must cover the overrun, and the refusal names the least and a round figure
    --extra-rounds N             Add N (a whole number from 1 up) to the review rounds the step may spend (its review.max_rounds), for a step that has spent them all; N must cover the overrun (1 for a step exactly spent), and the refusal names the least. Ignored, and nothing added, when the step still has rounds left or the resume does nothing. A usage error for a step with no review:
    --accept-guard               Accept the guard stop the run waits on (needs --note WHY)
    --retry                      With --accept-guard: run the stopped step again instead of passing it
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow resume RUN    # pick a stuck run up again: its lock is asked for again, a failed step runs again
  workspace workflow resume RUN --from implement    # start again at the implement step of rpiv
  workspace workflow resume RUN --note "The migration is already applied."    # tell the next attempt something
  workspace workflow resume RUN --pane %19    # the run's pane is gone: carry on in another pane of the workspace
  workspace workflow resume RUN --restart-step    # the step's agent or pane crashed: start it again in a fresh conversation
  workspace workflow resume RUN --extra-rounds 2    # a review spent its max_rounds: allow two more rounds and go on
  workspace workflow resume RUN --accept-guard --note "I rebased on purpose."    # accept a head_moved stop: the step's other checks run, measured from HEAD now
  workspace workflow resume RUN --accept-guard --retry --note "Hooks were updated upstream."    # accept the stop and run the step again
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow cancel --help

Usage: workspace workflow cancel [RUN] [--json]

End a run and release the locks it holds.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).
With RUN left out, the run this pane is bound to is used, else the one run going in this checkout; several going runs refuse with ambiguous_run and RUN is needed.

It does not type into the pane: the agent there is left as it is. A run that has ended is refused.
A step being reviewed has its round ended (the round's usage recorded) and its review window closed.

Options:
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow cancel RUN    # give up on a run that is going wrong; its locks are released
  workspace workflow cancel RUN    # end a run that waits at a gate you will not pass or for a lock you no longer need
  workspace workflow cancel RUN --json    # for a script: one action document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow pause --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow pause [RUN] [--interrupt] [--reason TEXT] [--json]

Hold a run: nothing new starts until you unpause it.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).
With RUN left out, the run this pane is bound to is used, else the one run going in this checkout; several going runs refuse with ambiguous_run and RUN is needed.

Pausing does not stop the agent's current turn unless you give --interrupt. When that turn ends, the run
holds instead of starting the next step. While paused, no step, retry or review round starts, and the
step's and round's time limits stop counting. Run `workflow unpause` to let it go on.

While paused, `workflow resume` (also one made from the run's own pane, which would wait for the
agent's turn to end) is refused (run_paused): unpause first. A resume already waiting is dropped. A run that has ended is refused (run_not_active), and so is one
already paused (already_paused).

With --interrupt, the agent's interrupt keys are pressed in the run's pane if the agent is working there, and
`interrupted` in --json says whether they were. `workflow unpause` then tells the agent to continue.
--interrupt is refused (bound_pane) from a pane bound to a run and from a process under the run's own pane.

Options:
    --interrupt                  Also press the agent's interrupt keys in the run's pane if the agent is working
    --reason TEXT                Why (1 to 4000 characters); kept with the pause and shown in status
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow pause RUN    # hold a run while you look at what it did
  workspace workflow pause RUN --interrupt --reason "wrong branch"    # stop the agent's turn too, and say why
  workspace workflow pause RUN --json    # for a script: one action document with outcome `paused` and `interrupted`
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow unpause --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow unpause [RUN] [--json]

Let a paused run go on, doing what the pause held.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).
With RUN left out, the run this pane is bound to is used, else the one run going in this checkout; several going runs refuse with ambiguous_run and RUN is needed.

Starts the step, line or review round the pause held back, or looks at a turn that ended while paused. If
`pause --interrupt` stopped the agent, it is told to continue once its pane is idle. An agent that is still
working is left alone. `unpaused` in --json says what was done: `action`, `held`, and `continued` or
`warning` when the agent was told to continue. It exits 0 even when that is still waiting for the pane, so a
script should check `continued` and `warning`. A run that is not paused is refused (not_paused), and so is
one that has ended (run_not_active). It is refused (bound_pane) from a pane bound to a run and from a
process under the run's own pane, so the run's agent cannot lift a person's pause.

Options:
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow unpause RUN    # let a run you paused carry on
  workspace workflow unpause RUN && workspace workflow status RUN    # carry on, then see what the unpause started
  workspace workflow unpause RUN --json    # for a script: one action document with the `unpaused` block
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow approve --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow approve [RUN] [--step STEP [--attempt N]] [--note-sha256 HEX] [--note TEXT] [--json]

Pass a run's gate.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).
With RUN left out, the run this pane is bound to is used, else the one run going in this checkout; several going runs refuse with ambiguous_run and RUN is needed.

Refused from a pane a run is bound to and from a process under the run's own pane, so an agent
doesn't pass its own plan by mistake. When the gated step's first file starts with `note: FILE`, the
note's sha256 is recorded and given to the next step. With --step (and --attempt) it is refused with
gate_not_waiting unless the run waits at that step's gate.

Options:
    --step STEP                  The gated step you saw (current.step in status --json); refused unless the run waits there
    --attempt N                  That step's attempt you saw (current.attempt); needs --step
    --note-sha256 HEX            The sha256 of the gate's note you read (gate_file.sha256); refused with stale_revision when it changed
    --note TEXT                  Added to the next attempt's instructions
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow approve RUN    # pass the gate a run waits at (`workflow status` shows it as waiting_you)
  workspace workflow approve RUN --note "Skip the migration."    # pass it and tell the next step something
  workspace workflow approve RUN --step plan --attempt 2    # pass it only if the run still waits at the plan step, attempt 2
  workspace workflow approve RUN --step plan --attempt 2 --note-sha256 HEX    # pass it only if the plan note is still the one you read (HEX is gate_file.sha256)
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow reject --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow reject [RUN] --note TEXT [--step STEP [--attempt N]] [--to STEP] [--extra-attempts N] [--extra-tokens N] [--extra-time DURATION] [--json]

Turn a run's gate down.

RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).
With RUN left out, the run this pane is bound to is used, else the one run going in this checkout; several going runs refuse with ambiguous_run and RUN is needed.

The gated step (or --to an earlier one) runs again with the note. Refused from a pane a run is bound
to and from a process under the run's own pane, as approve is. It is refused (attempts_spent) when
the run, or the step it would run, has made all its max_attempts (step_attempts_spent), unless
--extra-attempts N adds to the allowances; N must cover the overrun (1 for a run exactly spent). The
same goes for a spent token budget (budget_spent) and --extra-tokens N, and a spent run timeout
(run_timed_out) and --extra-time DURATION.

Options:
    --note TEXT                  Why; given to the next attempt
    --to STEP                    The step to run again (the gated step, or one before it)
    --step STEP                  The gated step you saw (current.step in status --json); refused unless the run waits there
    --attempt N                  That step's attempt you saw (current.attempt); needs --step
    --extra-attempts N           Add N (a whole number from 1 up) to the run's attempt allowance, for a run or step that has spent max_attempts; N must cover the overrun (1 for a run exactly spent), and the refusal names the least
    --extra-tokens N             Add N (a whole number from 1 up) to the run's token budget, for a run that has used budget.tokens; N must cover the overrun, and the refusal names the least and a round figure
    --extra-time DURATION        Add DURATION (30m, 2h, or seconds) to the run's timeout, for a run that has used its timeout: (active time is the time the machine was up, less waits for a person, stalls and downtime); DURATION must cover the overrun, and the refusal names the least and a round figure
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow reject RUN --note "Too big; split it."    # send the gated step back; it runs again with the note
  workspace workflow reject RUN --note "Research the API first." --to research    # go back to an earlier step of rpiv instead
  workspace workflow reject RUN --note "Too big; split it." --step plan --attempt 2    # turn it down only if the run still waits at the plan step, attempt 2
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace workflow advance --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace workflow advance RUN [--turn-ended --pane ID [--turn-started AT] [--stopped-at AT] [--background-task TYPE:ID]... [--transcript-path PATH]]

Move a run on; the agent daemon runs this when a turn ends.

It is not meant to be typed. RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`). It prints nothing.

Typed by hand it decides the run's step as the daemon would, so use `workflow resume` instead.

Options:
    --turn-ended                 A turn ended in the run's pane
    --pane PANE                  The run's pane
    --turn-started AT            When that turn began (ISO 8601)
    --stopped-at AT              When the daemon saw that turn end (ISO 8601)
    --background-task TYPE:ID    A background task still going when the turn ended (repeatable)
    --transcript-path PATH       The agent's transcript, for the status line its last message ends with
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow advance RUN    # nudge a stuck run: it waits on a lock, or its check never finished; it moves on if it can
  workspace workflow advance RUN --turn-ended --pane %19    # what the agent daemon runs when the agent in pane %19 finishes answering, so the run can go to its next step
  workspace workflow advance RUN --turn-ended --pane %19 --turn-started "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"    # the same, saying when that answer began
--- stderr
--- end

       workspace workflow approve [RUN] [--step STEP [--attempt N]] [--note-sha256 HEX] [--note TEXT] [--json]
       workspace workflow reject [RUN] --note TEXT [--step STEP [--attempt N]] [--to STEP] [--extra-attempts N] [--extra-tokens N] [--extra-time DURATION] [--json]

Run a workflow in a workspace: an ordered list of steps, each done by the agent in the
workspace's Claude pane. A step gets its instructions in a file under .workflow/ in the
checkout and one typed line pointing at it, in a fresh conversation unless the step says
context: continue. A step is done when the agent's turn ends, every file it produces:
is there (a non-empty regular file, not a link), and its status: check passes; the agent daemon (agentd) sees the turn end and
moves the run on. A failed step goes back along its on_fail: {goto, max}; a step with
gate: approve waits for `workflow approve`. Resources a step uses: are locks the run
holds, in the same queue as `lock acquire` and `dev up`.

Definitions are YAML files: $HOME/.config/workspace/workflows/ID.yml (a project's own, in $HOME/.config/workspace/projects/NAME/workflows/ID.yml, are found first; never read from a repository), then the directories of the workflows.sources config key in list order (source:1, source:2, ...), then the presets that
ship with workspace (rpiv: research, plan, implement, verify; rpiv-auto-approve: rpiv with reviewer agents in place of the plan gate; rpiv-auto-approve-v2: rpiv with the engine's own plan reviewers in place of the gate; pr-feedback: triage review feedback, then fix; investigate: reproduce, diagnose, fix; explore: read-only research, a gate, then a report note; bugfix (experimental): a failing test proven before a gate, then fix and verify). See docs/README.workflow.md.

  list           List the workflow definitions in a table (id, source, description)
  uninstall      Remove every workflow installed from the workflows.sources entries
  show           Print one workflow (its inputs and steps)
  graph          Draw a workflow's steps, gates, reviews and loops
  validate       Check a definition's text and list every problem
  add            Save a definition as ID.yml
  update         Replace your ID.yml if it is unchanged since you read it
  edit           Open a workflow's definition file in your editor
  remove         Delete your ID.yml
  install        Fetch and check the workflows.sources definitions
  run            Start a run of a workflow in a workspace
  render         Print the instructions a step's agent would be sent, without a run
  check          Run one step's status: check once, without a run
  simulate       Play a workflow through the real engine with a scripted fake agent and print the transitions
  start          Make a workspace from a ticket, pull request or prompt and run a workflow in it
  status         Show the runs still going, each with its step and why it is stuck
  attempts       Show what a run recorded about each attempt
  trace          Show a run as a timeline: every transition, its spans and where the time went
  audit          Check a run's kept evidence against the hashes recorded for it
  stats          Show how each step of a workflow went across its runs
  compare        Set a workflow's runs side by side, grouped by definition, version or pack text
  insights       Show where a workflow's recent runs keep retrying, being rejected or stopping
  learn reflect  Ask an agent in a new pane to look back at a finished run and write reflection.md
  sweep          One pass over the runs going: act on the ones that have stopped
  recover        Bring going runs back after a reboot
  events         Show a run's history, one line per event
  files          List the files a run keeps
  resume         Get a run going again
  cancel         End a run and release the locks it holds
  pause          Hold a run: nothing new starts until you unpause it
  unpause        Let a paused run go on, doing what the pause held
  approve        Pass a run's gate
  reject         Turn a run's gate down
Run `workspace workflow VERB --help` for a verb's options.

approve and reject with --step (and --attempt) are refused with gate_not_waiting unless the run
waits at that step's gate (on that attempt), so a stale button can't pass a later gate. These
checks guard against mistakes; they are not a security boundary (docs/README.workflow.md).

`workflow advance RUN [--turn-ended --pane ID [--turn-started AT] [--stopped-at AT] [--background-task TYPE:ID]... [--transcript-path PATH]]` is what the agent daemon runs to move a run
on when a turn ends; it is not meant to be typed.

`run` and `start` really start a run (start also makes a worktree); --dry-run checks and starts nothing.
`start` may leave out the ID: config names it (workflows.by_ref.<kind>, else workflows.default).
`run --file PATH` and `start --file PATH` run a definition file that is not installed (no ID with it); it names its own id (an `id:` key, or the file name), and you vouch for the file.
RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).

        --name WORKSPACE             run: the workspace to run in; render, check: the workspace whose packs and commands are read; show, validate, render, check, simulate, add, update, remove: the workspace whose project's definitions are read first (default: the current workspace); status: that workspace's runs still going (default: the current workspace); sweep: only that workspace's runs (default: every run going)
        --input KEY=VALUE            run, start, render, simulate: a value for one of the workflow's inputs (repeatable)
        --artifacts DIR              check: an existing directory standing for the run's artifacts (WORKSPACE_RUN_ARTIFACTS); default an empty temporary one
        --note TEXT                  run, start: added to every step's instructions; resume, approve, reject: to the next attempt's
        --pane PANE                  run, resume: the pane to run in (%19 or 0.1) instead of the workspace's Claude pane
        --from STEP                  resume: start again at this step
        --accept-guard               resume: accept the guard stop the run waits on (needs --note WHY); the checkout as it is now becomes the run's base and the step's other checks decide it
        --retry                      resume --accept-guard: run the stopped step again instead of passing it (a new attempt)
        --restart-step               resume: start a crashed step again in a fresh conversation
        --extra-attempts N           resume, reject: add N to the run's attempt allowance when it has spent max_attempts (ignored by a resume that starts no attempt)
        --extra-tokens N             resume, reject: add N to the run's token budget when it has used budget.tokens (ignored by a resume that starts no attempt)
        --extra-time DURATION        resume, reject: add DURATION (30m, 2h) to the run's timeout when it has used its timeout: (active time; ignored by a resume that starts no attempt)
        --extra-rounds N             resume: add N to the review rounds the step may spend (its review.max_rounds) when it has spent them all
        --interrupt                  pause: also press the agent's interrupt keys in the run's pane while it works
        --reason TEXT                pause: why (shown with the pause, at most 4000 characters)
        --to STEP                    reject: the step to run again (the gated step, or one before it)
        --step STEP                  approve, reject: the gated step you saw (current.step in status --json); refused unless the run waits there
        --attempt N                  approve, reject: that step's attempt you saw (current.attempt); needs --step
        --note-sha256 HEX            approve: the sha256 of the gate's note you read (gate_file.sha256); refused with stale_revision when it changed
        --script FILE                simulate: the YAML script of what the fake agent does on each attempt and how each check comes out
        --format FMT                 graph: how to draw it, mermaid, dot, ascii (default) or json
        --run RUN                    graph: draw the definition RUN stored, marked with each step's state and the loops it took
        --source                     show ID: the file's text, sha256 of its bytes and problems, valid or not; install: only the source at position N of workflows.sources (a whole number from 1, written after the flag)
        --attempt-of STEP            attempts, audit: only this step's attempts
        --by GROUP                   compare: group the runs by definition (default), version (the definition's `version:`) or pack:NAME, the text of that pack their agent was sent
        --agent KIND                 learn reflect: the coding agent the reflection pane runs: claude, codex, opencode, pi (default: the workspace's main agent)
        --limit N                    insights: read this many of the newest runs (default 20; a whole number from 1)
        --last DURATION              stats, compare, insights: only runs started in the last DURATION (30d, 2w, 12h, 90m; a run that started exactly then counts)
        --since N                    events: only events after line N of the history (default 0)
        --types A,B                  events: only events of these types (repeatable, or comma-separated)
        --timeout DURATION           events --follow: stop waiting after this long (30s, 5m, 1h) and exit 75
        --follow                     events: keep reading and print each event as it is appended, until the run has finished and its history is drained
        --id ID                      validate: check the text as this workflow id
        --project [NAME]             status: all runs of a project, finished too (NAME, or the project of the current workspace)
        --all                        status: every workspace's runs, finished too
        --needs-me                   status: the runs still going, in every workspace, that wait for you (a gate, question, prompt, failed check, gone pane, stall), each with the next command; --name or --project narrows it
        --table                      status: one row per run with its workspace's status and whether its config, tmux session, worktree and state directory exist; finished runs show at every scope; trace: one grid row per transition
        --ref REF                    start: run the workflow that fits REF's kind (workflows.by_ref.<kind>, then workflows.default, else the one that fits) instead of naming an ID
        --force                      start: start although the workflow's applies_to: does not list the REF's kind
        --dry-run                    run, start: report what would start and start nothing; sweep, recover: report what would be done and do nothing (sweep: also --install and --uninstall); add, update: check and write no definition (the lock file may be created); remove: check and delete nothing
        --install                    sweep: install the launchd entry that runs the sweep every 5 minutes (a per-user LaunchAgent; opt-in; a running agent daemon also sweeps its workspace every 5 minutes)
        --uninstall                  sweep: unload and remove that launchd entry
        --installed                  sweep: say whether that launchd entry is installed and loaded
        --budget-only                sweep: look only at token budgets with action: interrupt, and press only for one that is spent (the agent daemon runs this every minute for such runs; the full sweep runs every 5 minutes)
        --scheduled                  sweep: the pass the launchd entry runs; leaves each run whose workspace's agent daemon is running to that daemon (reason daemon_owns)
        --yes                        remove, uninstall: do not ask before deleting
        --if-sha256 SHA              update: the sha256 of the file's raw bytes you read; refuse with stale_workflow unless it still matches
        --prompt TEXT                start: the task as free text (the workflow's task input, and the branch's name when there is no REF)
        --branch BRANCH              start: the branch for a --prompt (default: the prompt's words); refused with a REF
        --slug                       start: add the ticket title's words to a JIRA or issue branch, as `workspace start --slug`
        --file PATH                  run, start: run the workflow definition in this YAML file instead of an installed ID (needs an `id:` key or an ID.yml name)
        --base REF                   start: the branch or ref a new branch starts from
        --[no-]headless              start: start the session in plain tmux, as `workspace start --headless`
        --agent-kind KIND            start: the coding agent the main agent pane runs: claude, codex, opencode, pi
        --prompt-timeout DURATION    start: how long to wait for the coding agent to be ready (default 60s)
        --turn-ended                 advance: a turn ended in the run's pane
        --group GROUP                advance --turn-ended: the fan_out group the run pane is bound to whole; the turn end judges every sibling still without an outcome
        --turn-started AT            advance: when that turn began (ISO 8601)
        --stopped-at AT              advance: when the daemon saw that turn end (ISO 8601)
        --background-task TYPE:ID    advance: a background task still going when the turn ended (repeatable)
        --transcript-path PATH       advance: the agent's transcript, for the status line its last message ends with
        --json                       Print one JSON document (see docs/README.workflow.md)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow show    # list the workflows you can run
  workspace workflow run rpiv --input task="PROJ-101 invoice PDF export" --dry-run    # check a run in this workspace and start nothing
  workspace workflow run rpiv --input task="PROJ-101 invoice PDF export"    # start it for real: step one is typed into the Claude pane
  workspace workflow start rpiv --prompt "add a hello script"    # make a worktree workspace from a sentence and run rpiv in it
  workspace workflow status    # which runs are going, and why one is stuck
  workspace workflow approve RUN --note "Skip the migration."    # pass the gate a run waits at
  workspace workflow reject RUN --note "Too big; split it."    # send the gated step back with a reason
  workspace workflow resume RUN --from implement    # start a stuck run again at one step
  workspace workflow cancel RUN    # end a run and release its locks
  workspace workflow pause RUN    # hold a run: nothing new starts until `workflow unpause RUN`
--- end
